sections.h2: Where is the Berrien County Register of Deeds and when can I record?
sections.html:
The office is in the Berrien County Administration Center at 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, Michigan 49085. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., except county holidays. Recording stops earlier, at 4:30 p.m., and public search terminals close at 4:45 p.m.

The phone number for questions is 269-983-7111, extension 8562. Berrien is the southwest corner county, with 8 cities, 9 villages and 22 townships on the county's own list, so deeds arrive from places as different as Benton Harbor, New Buffalo, Niles and Three Oaks.

  • Deliver originals in person, by courier, or by USPS, UPS or FedEx to 701 Main Street.
  • Include a self-addressed stamped envelope so the recorded document returns to the right party.
  • Only originals with original signatures are accepted. Photocopies are refused.
  • Payment is due in full at recording, made out to the Register of Deeds. The office cannot process checks meant for other county departments.

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Berrien County?
sections.html:
The county's fee page lists $30 to record a document regardless of page count, and its FAQ describes this as Michigan's flat fee per recordable event. A deed can also trigger a tax certification charge and transfer tax.

Berrien County Register of Deeds fees. Source: Berrien County fee page.
ItemCharge

Records search50 cents per year, $5 minimum

Warranty deeds, deeds with a warranty covenant, land contracts, land contract assignments and condominium master deeds must carry a tax certificate from the treasurer.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax will a Berrien County seller pay?
sections.html:
Berrien posts two rates for any non exempt deed worth $100 or more: the county tax is 55 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of it, and the state tax is $3.75 for each $500 or fraction. Together that is $4.30 per $500. The county also publishes a rate chart that breaks the figures down by sale price.

The full value has to be stated on the deed, or a real estate valuation affidavit must be attached. Any exemption must appear on the instrument itself.

Here is a worked example using the Census median owner occupied value for Berrien County of $224,300. That price holds 449 units of $500 once the fraction is rounded up. The state tax is 449 times $3.75, or $1,683.75. The county tax is 449 times 55 cents, or $246.95. The total at recording is $1,930.70. Ask the title agent how your contract splits the cost.

Exemptions under the state act include a deed from a parent to a child or from a grandparent to a grandchild, court orders without stated consideration, and transfers in a mortgage foreclosure. The county act covers many of the same cases but, as written, leaves out the family transfers, so confirm which tax applies before you sign.

sections.h2: What must a Berrien County document include to be recorded?
sections.html:
The office keeps a recording requirements page and answers common questions in its FAQ. The points below come up often with sellers and estates.

  • A death certificate must be a certified copy bearing the clerk's seal. Under MCL 565.48, bring it to record the death of a joint owner. The older deed stays the most recent deed of record until a new one is recorded.
  • Court documents need the court's certification and seal.
  • Notary service is available at the County Clerk, with appointments through ext. 8233 of the same main number, and also at banks, municipalities and title companies.
  • Staff cannot draft deeds. The office recommends an attorney or a title insurer, and notes that templates sold in office supply stores or online exist.
  • Mortgage survey reports are not filed here. Only a certified survey that was actually recorded will appear.

A recorded document is public. Anyone can buy a copy for $1 per page, and when a mortgage is paid off the lender records the discharge here.

sections.h2: How do I search Berrien County land records and use eRecording?
sections.html:
The county's Land Records Search page covers online lookups, and its separate e-Recording page covers electronic filing. A county property tax page also links the Register of Deeds online services alongside a transfer tax rate chart and a parcel split and combine flowchart.

Before a closing, run a name search to see the chain of title, open mortgages and any recorded liens. The statewide search charge is 50 cents per year searched. Parcel splits, which matter for a seller keeping part of a lot, are covered by the county's flowchart rather than by this office.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Berrien County?
sections.html:
QuickFacts estimates 152,444 residents for July 2025, a 1.3 percent drop from the 2020 base, across 567.78 square miles. There are 78,132 housing units and 63,999 households, with 72.8 percent of homes owner occupied.

The median owner occupied home value for 2020 to 2024 is $224,300 and median household income is $65,425. Owners with a mortgage pay a median $1,462 a month. About 13.8 percent of residents identify as Black alone and 7.9 percent speak a language other than English at home, which affects notary and interpreter needs at closings. Building permits for 2025 totaled 372.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee in Berrien County?
faqs.a: It is a flat $30 for each recordable document, whatever the page count. Add $3 for each additional instrument that one document assigns or discharges.

faqs.q: What are Berrien County's transfer tax rates?
faqs.a: The county rate is 55 cents per $500 of value and the state rate is $3.75 per $500, each counted by $500 or fraction. Exempt transfers must say so on the instrument.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Berrien County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the original with original signatures to 701 Main Street, St. Joseph, MI 49085, with full payment and a stamped return envelope. Photocopies cannot be recorded.

faqs.q: What time does Berrien County stop recording documents?
faqs.a: The office is open until 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, but documents are recorded between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. Public search terminals close at 4:45 p.m.

faqs.q: Does the Berrien County Register of Deeds notarize deeds?
faqs.a: No. The County Clerk has notaries, reachable on 269-983-7111 ext. 8233, and banks, municipalities and title companies also offer notary service, sometimes for a fee.
